name: Supertouch
label: Revelation
lede: A b-boy singer, a Bad Brains song title and a drummer poached from a dead band: Supertouch put funk, quiet parts and major chords into late-'80s New York hardcore and never got the credit.

eras.title: Death Before Dishonor, then a Bad Brains title
eras.text: Mark Ryan and Jon Biviano started out as DBD, with Mike Ferraro on drums when he was around. By the time Ferraro left for Youth of Today, the pair had a new drummer, a new bassist, and a name lifted from a Bad Brains song.

years.h: Mark Ryan and Jon Biviano start DBD in New York
years.p: Singer Mark Ryan and Jon Biviano, on bass at first, form Death Before Dishonor. [[Mike Ferraro|edffc714-f0a2-4d6c-b4c0-dc31e713481c]], later of [[Judge|3827fbb6-e219-4e2d-9af8-35cc9a7d8d8e]], plays drums when he can. Revelation dates Supertouch from here.

years.h: Two gigs with Mike Ferraro and Walter Schreifels
years.p: Jon Biviano says the band played two shows in spring 1987 with Mike Ferraro on drums and [[Walter Schreifels|9f350578-acdd-480e-8273-5eaf88842f1c]], soon of [[Gorilla Biscuits|0320a32e-b781-40df-bf48-5cb5ee842762]], on bass. Then Ferraro joined [[Youth of Today|9ca27db4-f127-4aeb-ae87-29e21f558c13]].

years.src: RevHQ: Jon Biv Part IV · Revelation Records
years.h: Andy Guida from Altercation, and the name Supertouch
years.p: Mark Ryan finds drummer Andy Guida, whose band Altercation had just folded; Mike Bitton takes bass. Named after a [[Bad Brains|e919b253-da5b-4aae-a444-6a368376a2d6]] song, Supertouch is official by September 1987.
years.xp:
Jon Biviano says Guida clicked at once: the new line-up got more done in two hours than in two years with Ferraro. Guida shared the band's impatience with the scene and could play far beyond straight-ahead hardcore.

Revelation's own bio singles out Ryan as one of hardcore's first b-boys, alongside Eddie Sutton of [[Leeway|121193a5-cb8b-4182-968c-8ba607856fa2]].

eras.title: Grooves nobody else in New York had
eras.text: Supertouch played quiet sections, major chords and funk-born improvisation in a scene that mostly wanted mosh parts. One 7" and one Revelation album caught it, and the band's WNYU tapes did the rest through the trading underground.

years.h: Supertouch play WNYU's Crucial Chaos on St. Patrick's Day
years.p: Mark Ryan, Jon Biviano, Andy Guida and Mike Bitton play seven songs live on WNYU's Crucial Chaos show. Most of them never appear on a Supertouch record.
years.xp:
Crucial Chaos ran Thursdays, 9 to 10:30 p.m. The set included Searching for the Light, True Colors Don't Run and Death in the Family.

The tape circulated among traders for two decades before Horror Hotel pressed it on vinyl in 2011. In Effect calls it the best document of the original line-up.

years.h: Searchin' for the Light on Revelation's New York comp
years.p: Supertouch land on Revelation's New York City Hardcore: The Way It Is, alongside [[Youth of Today|9ca27db4-f127-4aeb-ae87-29e21f558c13]], [[Gorilla Biscuits|0320a32e-b781-40df-bf48-5cb5ee842762]] and [[Sick of It All|e204ed91-3684-4561-b29b-d0b53f8459a7]].

years.h: Joe Graz answers a Village Voice ad and aces the tryout
years.p: Bassist Mike Bitton is out. Joe Graz, found through a Village Voice ad, learns all ten songs on the Supertouch demo before his audition, so it's barely a tryout at all.

years.h: What Did We Learn 7", Supertouch's first record
years.p: Supertouch's debut 7" comes out on Combined Effort, the one record between the WNYU tapes and the Revelation album.

years.h: Two Supertouch benefit shows in one day, two states
years.p: Jon Biviano recalls playing the Pipeline in Newark for radio station WFMU, then driving to the Anthrax in Connecticut to play for Amnesty International the same day.

years.src: Revelation Records · Some Will Never Know
years.p: Supertouch's only album of their first run: eleven songs, from Engine to Shame. How Do You Feel, first recorded in Connecticut in 1988, becomes their signature song.
years.xp: Revelation's writeup calls the record ahead of its time. The band had been pushing hardcore toward quiet parts, major chords and improvisation, and here it shows.

eras.title: Carpeted stages and a lost album
eras.text: With a new rhythm section, Supertouch toured Europe and kept writing, but the '90s wore them down. They stopped in 1996 with a second album, Guide to the Stars, finished and unreleased.

years.h: Bradford to Belgium overnight, then sleep on the stage
years.p: On a European tour, Supertouch play Bradford, England, load straight into the van for the Dover ferry, and arrive late at Vort'n Vis in Ieper, Belgium. They sleep on its carpeted stage.
years.xp:
The October–December 1992 tour was booked by Navigator, and Ieper was the band's only Belgian show. The line-up was Mark Ryan, Jon Biviano, drummer Rich Edsell and bassist Mark Randall.

The club fed them after the set and handed out Duvel, which Biviano says he still connects with Ieper.

years.h: Supertouch's bassist arrested in Utah on tour
years.p: Jon Biviano says the band's bass player was arrested in Utah in 1993 on drug paraphernalia charges.

years.big: A second album, left on the shelf
q: Would have fought harder to make sure Supertouch didn't stop.
years.src: Some Will Never Know · Supertouch Bandcamp
years.h: Supertouch stop, with Guide to the Stars unreleased
years.p: Supertouch quit playing in 1996. Their second album, Guide to the Stars, stays unreleased for well over a decade.
years.xp:
Jon Biviano has said he regrets letting the band stop. He went on to Windfall, a band with a female singer, from 1999 to 2003, and joined Running Like Thieves in 2000.

When Supertouch came back in 2010, the band tied it to historical releases, including Guide to the Stars.

eras.title: A surprise set at the Bowl
eras.text: A walk-on at the Black N' Blue Bowl turned into a real reunion: new songs, a 7", the old WNYU tape on vinyl, and the big hardcore festivals.

years.cap: Black N' Blue Bowl, New York, 2010
years.h: Supertouch's surprise set at the Black N' Blue Bowl
years.p: Fourteen years after they stopped, Supertouch walk on unannounced at New York's Black N' Blue Bowl. Mark Ryan and Jon Biviano decide to keep going.

years.h: Lost My Way 7": first new Supertouch in two decades
years.p: Four songs on Reaper Records, with Mark Ryan and Jon Biviano joined by Rich Edsell on drums and Dean Baltulonis on bass.

years.h: Horror Hotel presses Supertouch's 1988 WNYU set
years.p: After 23 years as a traded cassette, Supertouch's St. Patrick's Day 1988 set on WNYU finally comes out on vinyl through Horror Hotel.

years.h: Supertouch play America's Hardcore Fest in Cambridge
years.p: Supertouch take their late-'80s songs to America's Hardcore Fest in Cambridge, Massachusetts.
